subject.title: [Feature]: Pre-reset agentic memory flush — /new and daily reset should get the same memory flush as compaction

question: Should OpenClaw run a silent tool-capable memory flush against the outgoing session before explicit and automatic reset, and if so what default/config/security boundary should control it?
rationale: The requested behavior solves a real session-state/data-loss gap, but it changes default reset latency, model spend, tool execution, and sensitive memory persistence semantics across every user's daily/idle rollover.

options.title: Approve a gated core reset flush
options.body: Implement a bounded pre-reset agentic flush in the core reset path, with explicit timeout, empty-session/read-only/CLI guards, security review, and focused tests for `/new`, `/reset`, daily, and idle rollover.

options.title: Use plugin lifecycle hooks only
options.body: Keep core reset immediate and require memory plugins or hooks to persist reset context from `session_end`/`before_reset`, accepting that this will not be the same tool-capable agentic flush as compaction.

options.title: Defer to broader memory redesign
options.body: Leave this issue open as dependent on a larger memory-service or reset-continuity design rather than adding another lifecycle-specific flush path now.

recommendation.title: Approve a gated core reset flush
recommendation.body: Implement a bounded pre-reset agentic flush in the core reset path, with explicit timeout, empty-session/read-only/CLI guards, security review, and focused tests for `/new`, `/reset`, daily, and idle rollover.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest current-history owner for both the pre-compaction memory flush and the current reset/session initialization implementation.
